description: Two independent splitters, each sending a positive input to its P jack and a negative one to its N jack as a positive value

inputs.text: The signal split by the upper pair of jacks; the voltage is clamped to -10V to 10V before anything else
The signal split by the lower pair of jacks; the voltage is clamped to -10V to 10V before anything else

outputs.text: Carries the upper input whenever that is zero or above, and 0V whenever it is below; the maker's tooltip on this jack says IN2, which is the lower input's name
Carries the size of the upper input whenever that is below zero, as a positive voltage, and 0V whenever it is at or above zero; the maker's tooltip on this jack says IN2
Carries the lower input whenever that is zero or above, and 0V whenever it is below
Carries the size of the lower input whenever that is below zero, as a positive voltage, and 0V whenever it is at or above zero

notes: no output ever goes negative; a negative input arrives at the N jack as its absolute value
the two halves share nothing; each has its own input, its own pair of outputs and its own menu setting
with an input unpatched both of its outputs are held at 0V on one channel
polyphony is passed through: each half sets its two outputs to the channel count of its own input and splits every channel on its own sign
menu: UPPER PART: — the three items below this heading set what the upper half puts out
Keep IN1 voltage (default) — the upper half passes the voltage itself, negative ones flipped positive
Force outputs to +5V — the upper half puts out a flat 5V on whichever jack is active, so it becomes a sign detector
Force outputs to +10V — the upper half puts out a flat 10V on whichever jack is active
LOWER PART: — the three items below this heading set what the lower half puts out
Keep IN2 voltage (default) — the lower half passes the voltage itself, negative ones flipped positive
Force outputs to +5V — the lower half puts out a flat 5V on whichever jack is active
Force outputs to +10V — the lower half puts out a flat 10V on whichever jack is active
